label: context.reference
text:
Use the connected Firecrawl Application through its bound world_mcp_firecrawl interface and current MCP catalog. Select web search, scrape, map, crawl or extraction tools from the task and the server's actual schemas. For research, search first with firecrawl_search, then scrape the chosen results with firecrawl_scrape. On a large site, run firecrawl_map before firecrawl_crawl; poll a started crawl with firecrawl_check_crawl_status.

Current capabilities are declared in mcp.operation_catalog, mcp.tool_catalog, mcp.resource_catalog, mcp.resource_templates and mcp.prompt_catalog from world_mcp_firecrawl; send requests with label mcp.operation.request. When Firecrawl was connected in Octopus, each server tool is also published as its own firecrawl.<tool> operation. The declared operations also include firecrawl.call_tool with the catalog tool name and arguments, firecrawl.read_resource, firecrawl.get_prompt and firecrawl.complete. Use firecrawl.status or firecrawl.ping when connection state is uncertain.

Server tools not declared read-only wait for the operator's approval in Octopus before they reach the server. Their mcp.tool.result arrives after the operator decides; a declined call returns error operator_declined and changed nothing. Do not repeat a call while it waits.

Inspect the returned MCP content and error status when interpreting the result. Keep the API key inside its owning interface; use returned handles and status information.
